scope: Retaining versus regenerating full recursive public-key zero columns after the earlier error-absorbing binary-key transport.
limitations: Finite diagnostic, not a Lean theorem, full bootstrap trial, or security attack. Diagnostic bounded errors are not an asymptotic LWE hardness instantiation. Selected encryption columns use independent binary subset selectors and the constant-feature top gadget column; the nearest-codeword decoder breaks ties toward zero as in the Lean definition. Exhaustive key enumeration is unbounded. The support bounds do not exclude changing the public table by another joint nonlinear simulator, or a game-specific uniform endpoint that has no valid decryption key.

mathematical_bounds.retained_wrong_key: For independent fresh columns under s, any fixed binary v != s has independent uniform phases: coefficient of one inner mask is s_i-v_i = +/-1. With H < q/2, compatibility is ((2H+1)/q)^p.
mathematical_bounds.retained_adaptive_key: A union bound over all wrong binary keys bounds existence by (2^n-1)((2H+1)/q)^p, also covering adaptive key selection.
mathematical_bounds.uniform_full_table: For each binary v, the independently uniform body makes every column phase uniform. Existence of any compatible binary key has probability at most 2^n((2H+1)/q)^p.
mathematical_bounds.regeneration_endpoint: A sampler always producing a compatible binary key and narrow-noise zero table is separated in TV from a uniform full table by at least 1-2^n((2H+1)/q)^p. This separating event may be computationally infeasible to test.
